proposals.title: Spatially-Aware Domain Segmentation
proposals.summary: This analysis involves applying a clustering approach that integrates both gene expression profiles and spatial coordinates to segment a tissue into biologically meaningful regions. By leveraging spatial-aware distance measures and local neighborhood information, the method aims to reduce over-fragmentation of domains and account for natural transitions at tissue boundaries. The study would compare performance with standard clustering techniques, focusing on the accurate identification of sharp tissue boundaries versus gradual transitions.

proposals.title: Gradient and Boundary Transition Analysis
proposals.summary: In this analysis, we will compute spatial gradients of gene expression across tissue sections to identify areas of abrupt changes that indicate biological boundaries and gradual variations that suggest transitional regions. The method employs differential spatial smoothing that preserves local heterogeneity without inducing biases. The impacts of sampling resolution and sparse transcript measurements on boundary detection are carefully evaluated.

proposals.title: Cross-Section Integration for 3D Tissue Reconstruction
proposals.summary: This analysis targets the integration of spatial transcriptomics data collected from consecutive tissue sections to reconstruct three-dimensional tissue architecture. The procedure involves aligning sections using spatial coordinates and correcting for section-specific batch effects. The evaluation will assess coherence in the reconstructed 3D domains, accounting for both gene expression continuity and anatomical consistency across sections.

proposals.title: Joint Low-Dimensional Embedding Using Expression and Neighborhoods
proposals.summary: Here, we develop an analysis that learns a low-dimensional embedding by combining high-dimensional gene expression profiles with local spatial neighborhood information. Dimensionality reduction techniques such as spatially informed principal component analysis or autoencoders will be used to create representations robust to technical variations, allowing for enhanced visualization and clustering of tissue regions while preserving local spatial relationships.

proposals.title: Boundary-Preserving Adaptive Smoothing
proposals.summary: This analysis focuses on the application of adaptive smoothing techniques that dynamically adjust smoothing parameters based on local spatial gradients to avoid blurring important boundaries. The method involves tuning parameters in a region-specific manner to optimally suppress noise without compromising sharp gene expression transitions. The performance of this approach will be benchmarked against traditional smoothing methods.

proposals.title: Near-Boundary Expression Profiling
proposals.summary: The analysis explores gene expression patterns specifically in zones that flank the boundaries between tissue regions. It involves defining spatial buffer zones around domain borders to study how expression levels of key marker genes change across these transitions. Statistical models are then used to evaluate the degree of mixing or dissociation between domains, highlighting the biological significance of boundary gradients.

proposals.title: Multi-Resolution Spatial Transcriptomics Integration
proposals.summary: The analysis aims to integrate findings from spatial transcriptomics datasets generated at multiple resolutions—ranging from multicellular capture spots to near single-cell resolution—to provide a unified view of tissue architecture. It involves scaling strategies for aligning data from different platforms, as well as assessments of the impact of resolution on the detection of subtle spatial expression patterns and tissue segmentation.

proposals.title: Spatial Deconvolution of Cell Mixtures
proposals.summary: This proposal seeks to deconvolve the contributions of multiple cell types present in each spatial capture spot by integrating reference single-cell transcriptomic profiles with spatial transcriptomics data. Advanced statistical deconvolution methods will be used to estimate cell-type proportions in heterogeneous regions, highlighting how cell composition correlates with spatial domain boundaries and tissue architecture.

proposals.title: Spatial Domain Reconstruction using Graph-Based Models
proposals.summary: This analysis applies graph-based modeling to represent spatial transcriptomics data, where nodes represent capture spots and edges capture local spatial relationships. Community detection algorithms on this graph structure are employed to identify coherent spatial domains and uncover long-range spatial interactions. This method emphasizes the balance between local neighborhood effects and global tissue patterning to reconstruct biologically relevant domains.
